newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan activists plan to disrupt Israel trade fair.
newsitem.headline: Jordan activists plan to disrupt Israel trade fair.

text.p: Jordanians campaigning against the first Israeli trade fair in Amman said they will form a human shield to prevent it from going ahead on Wednesday.

Former Prime Minister and intelligence chief Ahmed Obeidat, who heads the campaign, told Reuters on Tuesday: "Jordanian men and women are determined to prevent the fair from taking place in a peaceful and democratic protest, expressing their resistance to normalisation with Israel."
Security sources confirmed that police were ordered to assume a state of alert to ensure public peace was maintained. Heavy security would also be set up near Amman's international exhibition centre.

Obeidat, who said supporters would try to block people from entering the exhibition, heads a national committee that represents a broad-based coalition of parties and unions opposed to the exhibition.
The group reflects the strength of anti-Israeli feelings among many Jordanians who still shun contacts despite the 1994 peace treaty that ended a 46-year state of war.
But appeal to the government to cancel the fair has gone unheeded.
The government "is not forcing ties with Israelis down peoples' throats" said one official.

Powerful business groups, pro-government and Islamist political parties, along with 11 main professional unions representing over 100,000 members, have published appeals in newspapers calling on Jordanians to block the fair.
Even the 350-strong journalists' union called on colleagues not to cover the four day event.

"This fair is an affront to peoples feelings in Jordan, as all what Israel is doing on the ground is destroying the concept of peace and destroying the hopes of peoples in the region of peace," Obeidat said.
Fakhri Naser, exhibition organiser, said the demands did not "represent the man in the street".
"I am adamant about going ahead...no way will I back down now," he told Reuters.

Naser said around 70 Israeli companies have booked 1,500 square metres display space on the exhibition's site, adding that over 12,000 invitations have been distributed to interested businessmen, including Gulf Arabs keen to view Israeli products.

More than 200 Israeli businessmen were expected to attend the exhibition and display products from a wide section of Israeli industry, including high tech products, garments, jewellery, chemicals and furniture, he said.
